lessonRef.title: Synthesis and review: auto personal and mortgage loan concepts
lessonRef.focus: auto personal and mortgage loan concepts

objective: Learners discover that different invented rate-and-term combinations can produce identical total interest, and reason about what still separates them.
scenario: Nerissa is a made-up eighth grader comparing two pretend $12,000.00 loans: 6% simple interest over three years, and 9% simple interest over two years. All figures are invented, and both use simple interest rather than the amortising schedules real loans normally follow.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Compute one simulated year of interest on Nerissa's first invented loan at 6%.

prompts.text: How much interest does the 6% loan accrue in a year?

tasks.directions: Extend each of Nerissa's loans over its own term and compute the total interest for each.

prompts.text: What is the total interest on the 6% loan over three years?
What is the total interest on the 9% loan over two years?

tasks.directions: Compare Nerissa's two loans on total repayment and on how long the debt is carried.

prompts.text: What is repaid in total on the 9% two-year loan?
What is the difference in total repayment between the two loans?
Nerissa's two loans cost the same in total. Give two reasons a borrower might still strongly prefer one over the other.

remediation: If a learner assumes the higher rate must cost more, compute both of Nerissa's totals fully before any conclusion is stated.
extension: Ask the learner what term at 9% would make Nerissa's second loan cheaper than the first, and to show the method.
